findings.text: render_trip_panels.py:60 _saddles re-implements stationary-point finding that nova/equilibrium/display_flux.py:172 _stationary_saddle already owns, and in a weaker form: the local version samples a 33x33 lattice with a sign test on the raw Hessian and no polish, so the saddle flux feeding the bounding surface is a grid-level candidate rather than a stationary point. The manifest names this under rubric.record but the fragment's bounding surface rests on it.

_bilinear is named for bilinear interpolation but resolves the point to the nearest grid cell with int(round(...)); every axis flux, limiter flux and saddle flux quoted in per-trip-panels.json is therefore a nearest-cell sample. A reader of the name would not expect that error term.
_edge_flux is defined and never called; dead code in a landed script.

figure.suptitle(...) puts a title on the figure, against the repository's binding plotting rule that the caption carries identity and the figure needs no title or suptitle (nova AGENTS.md, data-ink rules). Three SVGs were committed with it.

done_when item 3 names the bounding surface from nova.equilibrium.connectivity_boundary.host_boundary_read; the fragment draws a reduced derivation instead. The substitution is stated in the text, so it is disclosed rather than hidden, but the named routine is not exercised.
